components.name: Primary Button

components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; background: #B8860B; color: #fff; font-family: 'DM Sans', sans-serif; font-weight: 500; font-size: 0.875rem; padding: 10px 16px; border: none; border-radius: 8px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 150ms cubic-bezier(0,0,0.2,1), transform 100ms; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #8B6508; } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.97); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #B8860B; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; } .ds-btn-icon { width: 16px; height: 16px; }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: Secondary action. Transparent with parchment border.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; background: transparent; color: #1A1A16; font-family: 'DM Sans', sans-serif; font-weight: 500; font-size: 0.875rem; padding: 10px 16px; border: 1px solid #E8E4DC; border-radius: 8px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 150ms; } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: #FFFDF7; } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #B8860B; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Standard form field. White fill, parchment border, gold focus ring.
components.css: .ds-field { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 6px; } .ds-label { font-family: 'DM Sans', sans-serif; font-weight: 500; font-size: 0.75rem; color: #1A1A16; letter-spacing: 0.01em; } .ds-input { background: #fff; border: 1px solid #E8E4DC; border-radius: 8px; padding: 10px 12px; font-family: 'DM Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; color: #1A1A16; width: 100%; box-sizing: border-box; transition: box-shadow 150ms; outline: none; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #6B6860; } .ds-input:focus { box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #B8860B; } .ds-input:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; }

narrative.overview:
This is a tool that handles other people's gold. The interface must feel like it was made to the same standard as what it manages: minimal weight, maximum trust, nothing ornamental. The vault door aesthetic is not cold or corporate — it is calm confidence. Everything placed with intention. Nothing there by accident.

The gold accent (#B8860B) is not decoration. It is the combination. It appears at the active state, the primary action, and the amount that matters. Its rarity is the point.

This system explicitly rejects: the ledger anxiety of Tally-style accounting software, the aggression of fintech dashboards (gradients, glows, dark mode by default), and the forgettable genericness of SaaS admin panels.
keyCharacteristics: Flat surfaces with warm tints — depth through tonal contrast, never box-shadows at rest
Two-font system: DM Serif Display for financial amounts; DM Sans for all operational text
Gold earns every pixel it occupies
Indian rupee formatting (₹1,20,000) always; amounts are never small, never truncated

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: The gold accent is used on ≤10% of any given screen. Its rarity is the point.

rules.name: The Warm Neutral Rule
rules.body: Every surface, border, and divider must be tinted warm. Cold grey is a foreign element.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: A card at rest has a border and a warm white background. That is all. Shadow on hover only.

rules.name: The Serif Amount Rule
rules.body: DM Serif Display is reserved for rupee amounts and primary headings only. Its scarcity gives financial figures their weight.

rules.name: The Mono Code Rule
rules.body: Item codes (NEC0042) are always in monospace gold type. They are identifiers, not text.

rules.name: The Amount Visibility Rule
rules.body: Rupee amounts are never truncated, never in muted color when they are primary information.

rules.name: The Badge Never Alone Rule
rules.body: OVERDUE badges must always appear with an explicit day count alongside.

rules.name: The No Nested Cards Rule
rules.body: Cards do not contain cards. Use border-top dividers or background tints to group within a card.

dos: Do use DM Serif Display exclusively for rupee amounts and primary headings
Do display rupee amounts in Indian number formatting — ₹1,20,000 not ₹120,000
Do show deposit refund in a visually dominant gold-tinted panel on the return screen
Do use warm neutral tints (#E8E4DC borders, #FFFDF7 cards) throughout
Do accompany every OVERDUE badge with an explicit day count in text
Do enforce 44×44px minimum tap targets on all interactive elements
Do display item codes in monospace gold type above ornament names
Do keep the gold accent under 10% of any screen's surface area
donts: Don't use box-shadow on cards at rest — depth comes from background tints only
Don't use border-left or border-right greater than 1px as a colored accent stripe
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text with gradient)
Don't build screens that look like Tally or legacy ERP software
Don't build screens that resemble fintech or crypto dashboards
Don't use generic SaaS admin panel defaults
Don't truncate rupee amounts — change the layout if it doesn't fit
Don't use cold grey (#E5E7EB) anywhere — use warm parchment (#E8E4DC)
Don't use emoji in button labels, headings, or navigation
